text: So is paying people always a mistake? Not at all. Here's when it worked.

In 1932, wheat farmers in Western Australia — many of them war veterans, already hit by the Depression — watched around twenty thousand emus eat their crops. The army sent soldiers with two machine guns. At a farm dam, over a thousand emus walked into a perfect ambush. The gun killed about a dozen... and jammed. They mounted a gun on a truck. The emus outran the truck. The Major reported 986 kills with 9,860 rounds — his own count.

When farmers asked for soldiers again in 1934, the answer was no. What actually worked was older and cheaper: a cash bounty, paid to farmers for each emu. In six months of 1934, farmers filed over fifty-seven thousand bounty claims.
The difference? The bounty paid for the thing the farmers actually wanted gone: the emu. Not a tail. Not a barcode. Not an account. The real result.
